newsitem.title: JAPAN: Forex-driven export surge revs up Japan car output.
newsitem.headline: Forex-driven export surge revs up Japan car output.

text.p: Japanese vehicle production surged by almost 16 percent last month as factories rolled out more cars to meet export demand triggered by the weaker yen, an industry body said on Tuesday.

The Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association, which compiled the data, also said it expected production to keep rising for a while, although industry analysts expect the pace to slow down later this year.
Brisk car exports have been a major factor pushing up Japan's politically sensitive trade surplus and spurring fears of trade friction with the United States.
Vehicle production rose in May despite sluggish domestic demand following a rise in Japan's sales tax in April.

The association said domestic vehicle production climbed 15.8 percent from a year earlier to 890,611 vehicles, rising for the third straight month on a year-on-year basis as a relatively weaker yen made Japanese goods more price-competitive overseas.
"The increase in May resulted mainly from higher exports," an association official said, adding that there should be further year-on-year gains in the coming months.
"We expect Japan's vehicle production to remain high for a while as exports remained slow in the first half of last year."

The industry body also said it expected figures for Japan's vehicle exports in May, due later this week, to show a rise of about 30 percent from a year earlier, partly because Japan had comparatively low exports in May last year.
Analysts expect output to slow down later in the year, as political pressures are likely to limit export growth.
"I am sure Japanese carmakers will revise (down) their vehicle production by autumn," said Seiji Sugiura, a car industry analyst at Nomura Securities Co Ltd's research unit.
Japan's overall vehicle production in the year to March 1998 is likely to be between 10.50 million and 10.70 million units, against an actual 10.60 million units the previous year, Sugiura said.

Japanese carmakers' production plans in 1997/98 are too optimistic and they cannot boost their exports substantially because of calls at the Group of Seven (G7) summit for Japan to reduce its trade surplus, he said.

An official at Japan's Trade Ministry said on Monday that Japan's crude steel production in the third quarter of 1997/98 ending in December was likely to remain flat against estimated output of 26.05 million tonnes in the July-September period because of the expected slowdown in car production.
